contract_plain_english: [PDF p. 9, printed p. 913; anchor: Lemma 2.1 and proof] In exact arithmetic, if A and its sketch SA have full column rank and R is the triangular factor of the economized QR of SA, then right-preconditioning A by the exact inverse R^{-1} gives precisely the same spectral condition number as restricting the sketch S to the column space of A, namely kappa_2(AP) = kappa_2(SQ_A).

source_evidence.observation: For A in R^{m x n} with linearly independent columns, S in R^{s x m} with s >= n and linearly independent rows, B = SA, economized QR factorizations A = Q_A R_A and B = QR, and P = R^{-1}, the lemma states kappa_2(AP) = kappa_2(SQ_A).
The proof uses AP = Q_A R_A R^{-1}, B = SA = QR = S(Q_A R_A), and (SQ_A)R_A R^{-1} = Q with Q orthonormal.

source_evidence.anchor: Paragraphs immediately before and after Lemma 2.1
source_evidence.observation: The identity is explicitly presented as an exact-arithmetic property of the Blendenpik preconditioner, not as a finite-precision or probabilistic equality.
The paper assumes throughout that A and SA are full rank, with m > s > n in the main least-squares setting.
The paper defines kappa_2 as sigma_max divided by sigma_min.

statement.algorithm_linkage: [PDF p. 9, printed p. 913; anchor: prose immediately before Lemma 2.1] This is the exact-arithmetic condition-number identity for Blendenpik's sketch-and-precondition construction: sketch A to SA, take R from its QR factorization, and use P = R^{-1} as the right preconditioner.
binders: [PDF p. 9, printed p. 913; anchor: Lemma 2.1 statement] A in R^{m x n}, S in R^{s x m}, B := SA in R^{s x n}, and dimensions satisfying s >= n.

[PDF p. 9, printed p. 913; anchor: Lemma 2.1 statement] A = Q_A R_A and B = QR are economized QR factorizations, with Q_A in R^{m x n}, Q in R^{s x n}, and square upper-triangular R_A and R in R^{n x n}.
[PDF p. 9, printed p. 913; anchor: Lemma 2.1 statement] P := R^{-1} is the exact right preconditioner.
conclusions: [PDF p. 9, printed p. 913; anchor: Lemma 2.1 displayed conclusion] kappa_2(AP) = kappa_2(SQ_A), where P = R^{-1}.
[PDF p. 9, printed p. 913; anchor: proof of Lemma 2.1] The proof establishes the intermediate equalities kappa_2(AP) = kappa_2(R_A R^{-1}) and kappa_2(R_A R^{-1}) = kappa_2(SQ_A).
[PDF p. 9, printed p. 913; anchor: proof identity] The second equality is supported by (SQ_A)R_A R^{-1} = Q with Q having orthonormal columns.
constants_and_indexing: [PDF p. 9, printed p. 913; anchor: Lemma 2.1 statement] The only dimension constraint printed locally is s >= n; there are no numerical constants, iteration indices, or index offsets in the identity.
[PDF p. 9, printed p. 913; anchor: Lemma 2.1 displayed equation] The equality has no multiplicative distortion factor: the two condition numbers are exactly equal.
definitions_and_conventions: [PDF p. 9, printed p. 913; anchor: prose before Lemma 2.1] Q_A is an orthonormal basis for the column space of A.
[PDF p. 9, printed p. 913; anchor: Lemma 2.1 statement] "Economized QR" uses n-column orthonormal factors and n-by-n triangular factors for the full-column-rank matrices.
[PDF p. 2, printed p. 906; anchor: definition of kappa_2(A)] kappa_2(M) := sigma_max(M)/sigma_min(M) for the full-column-rank matrices in the identity.
[PDF p. 9, printed p. 913; anchor: Lemma 2.1 statement] P is the mathematical inverse R^{-1}, not a separately rounded or approximately computed inverse.
error_notions: [PDF p. 9, printed p. 913; anchor: Lemma 2.1 statement and proof] The result contains no forward error, backward error, residual, or computed-value error claim; it is solely an exact condition-number identity.

[PDF p. 9, printed p. 913; anchor: condition-number identity] A, AP, and SQ_A must have nonzero smallest singular values for the finite condition numbers used in the proof.
[PDF p. 9, printed p. 913; anchor: exact-arithmetic discussion] Floating-point exceptional values, overflow, underflow, NaNs, and infinities are outside the claim.
